# Rust security backports

`glib-0.18.5/` is one shared, source-patched copy of the published MIT-licensed
GTK-rs GLib crate. Both desktop Cargo roots use it through `[patch.crates-io]`:

- `apps/professional-desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`:
  `../../../vendor/rust/glib-0.18.5`;
- `apps/labs/semantica/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`:
  `../../../../vendor/rust/glib-0.18.5`.

The patch fixes [GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g)
without changing the 0.18 crate version, public API, features, or GTK ABI. See
[the backport receipt](glib-0.18.5/SECURITY-BACKPORT.md) for source provenance.
The original upstream README, COPYRIGHT, LICENSE, and source are retained.
No build outputs, registry cache metadata, or local Cargo credentials belong
in this directory.

## Maintenance and proof

The security-remediation owner maintains this backport until a compatible
upstream fixed release or supported Tauri/GTK dependency migration replaces
it. New upstream glib versions must be assessed together with GTK/WebKit/Tauri
constraints; adding a second glib version does not replace the vulnerable one.

The four `security_variant_str_iter_` tests exercise forward and reverse
iteration, mixed ends with nth/nth_back, empty arrays, empty/Unicode strings,
and out-of-bounds skips. Run the optimized form because compiler optimization
exposed the original undefined behavior. From the repository root:

```sh
cargo test --release --manifest-path vendor/rust/glib-0.18.5/Cargo.toml \
  --target-dir "$HOME/.cache/beep/glib-security-backport-target" \
  --lib security_variant_str_iter_
```

Also run the retained upstream iterator suite, and resolve/build/test both
application roots with their production GTK/WebKit features. Inspect both
Cargo-generated locks and dependency chains to establish that both use this
one patched source and do not retain a registry glib 0.18.5 alongside it.
Source patching, compilation, runtime behavior, advisory scanners, and GitHub
alert closure are separate claims. The unchanged crate version may remain
flagged by version-only scanners; do not fake a version or checksum to silence
that result.

After PR #1928 merged, both locks were regenerated by Cargo. Both application
roots passed locked production-feature checks and library tests; all four
security iterator tests passed in release mode. The packet Rust report records
commands, results, compiler warnings, and the remaining runtime/closure boundary.

## Reversal and retirement

Keep this vendor tree, the two manifest patch entries, both generated lock
changes, and provenance in one reviewable backport commit inside the combined
security PR. To reverse that backport, revert its commit: restore both prior
locks and manifests and remove this source. Rebuild both application roots.
That restores the known vulnerable baseline; use it only as a recovery route,
not a completed security disposition.

Prefer retirement through a fixed compatible upstream release or supported
GTK/Tauri migration. Remove both patch entries and this source together,
generate both locks through Cargo, repeat the optimized regression and both
application checks, then retain the provenance receipt in packet history.
